title: DMM reading-plus-range accuracy bound
description: Convert a manufacturer's DC voltage accuracy specification into separate gain and range contributions and a worst-case reading interval.
formula: E_read = abs(V_read) a/100; E_range = V_range b/100; E = E_read + E_range; V_low,high = V_read +/- E
assumptions: The specification uses percent of reading plus percent of the selected positive full-scale range, not percent of the bipolar span or display counts.
The stated coefficients apply at the actual temperature, calibration age, integration setting and measurement function. Additional specified errors must already be accounted for.
The interval is a specification error bound, not a confidence interval or standard uncertainty. Loading and lead errors are excluded.

references.title: Keithley E-Handbook to Understanding Electrical Test and Measurement, Step 2: Accuracy and Instrumentation error

constraints.message: Reading must lie within the selected full-scale range; overrange specifications are outside this model

title: Three-point delta resistance and thermal-EMF rejection
description: Recover resistance from equally spaced +I, -I, +I four-wire readings while canceling constant and linearly drifting thermoelectric voltage.
formula: V_R = (V1-2 V2+V3)/4; R = V_R/I; E_mid = (V1+2 V2+V3)/4; dE/dt = (V3-V1)/(2 delta_t)
assumptions: The three readings are equally spaced by delta_t, at settled currents +I, -I, +I of equal magnitude. Voltage lead polarity does not reverse.
DUT is an ohmic, nonnegative resistance with negligible change from self-heating during the cycle; four-wire sensing excludes force-lead drops.
Thermoelectric EMF is linear over the cycle. Quadratic drift, current mismatch, unsettled switching transients and voltage noise are not canceled.

references.title: Keithley Low-Voltage Measurement Techniques, The Delta Method of Measuring Resistance and Equipment Requirements

constraints.message: Readings must imply a nonnegative ohmic resistance with the stated voltage polarity

title: Compensated passive probe with source loading
description: Solve a passive oscilloscope probe's two parallel-RC divider sections with finite DUT source resistance, including compensation and frequency-dependent loading.
formula: tp=Rp Cp; ti=Ri Ci; A=Rs+Rp+Ri; B=Rs(tp+ti)+Rp ti+Ri tp; C=Rs tp ti; H(jw)=Ri(1+jw tp)/(A-w^2 C+jw B); Cp_match=Ri Ci/Rp
assumptions: Probe section Rp parallel Cp lies between DUT tip and scope node; Ri parallel Ci lies between scope node and ground. Ci includes scope and lumped cable capacitance.
Source is an ideal sinusoidal Thevenin voltage behind real Rs. Source voltage and output are peak magnitudes.
The cable is electrically short and its inductance, transmission-line behavior, probe loss, ground-lead inductance and oscilloscope amplifier bandwidth are negligible at the selected frequency.
Equal RC time constants flatten tip-to-scope attenuation, not source-to-scope attenuation when Rs is nonzero. This is not a probe safety or bandwidth rating.

references.title: University of Cincinnati ECECS 349 Measurements Lab: Accurate Measurements with an Oscilloscope, Figures 1-3
Tektronix ABCs of Probes Primer, Zero Signal Source Loading; Compensate Your Probes; Input Impedance

outputs.label: Capacitance for equal RC time constants
Scope input peak voltage before readout scaling

title: Rectangular measurement-aperture response
description: Calculate sinusoidal attenuation and time attribution from uniform integration over a finite measurement aperture, including DC and zero-aperture limits.
formula: x=pi f T; H(f)=exp(-j pi f T) sinc(x); sinc(x)=sin(x)/x, sinc(0)=1; Vout_peak=Vin_peak abs(sinc(x)); delay=T/2
assumptions: Measurement is a continuous, uniformly weighted boxcar average over the preceding aperture T; the reported sample timestamp is the aperture end.
The signed gain is referenced to the aperture midpoint. A negative signed gain adds a polarity inversion beyond the aperture-end delay.
No discrete-sampling alias, quantization, acquisition settling, jitter, additional analog response, or nonuniform weighting is included.
T=0 represents ideal instantaneous measurement. Nulls have zero mathematical amplitude; no logarithmic attenuation is returned, so nulls remain in the domain.

references.title: NI Adjusting the Reading Rate of a DMM, DMM Measurement Cycle and Aperture Time

outputs.label: Signed gain relative to aperture midpoint

title: Sinusoidal sampling-jitter noise limit
description: Predict input-referred sampling error and jitter-only SNR from analog signal slope and measured total RMS sampling-time uncertainty.
formula: sigma_phase=2 pi f sigma_t; Verror_rms=Vpeak sigma_phase/sqrt(2); SNR_jitter=-20 log10(2 pi f sigma_t)
assumptions: Input is a sinusoid and sampling-time error has zero mean, is independent of signal phase, and is represented by total RMS jitter over the relevant measurement bandwidth.
First-order slope approximation; RMS phase error is at most 0.1 rad. For Gaussian jitter this bounds the RMS-error linearization bias to approximately 0.125 percent.

Jitter-only SNR excludes quantization, thermal noise, spurs, deterministic coherent timing modulation and analog distortion. Do not substitute peak-to-peak or period jitter for RMS aperture-time uncertainty.
Frequency, amplitude and jitter are positive because a noise-free or zero-signal SNR is not finite; use the aperture model for deterministic DC response.

references.title: Texas Instruments SNAP004, PLL Fundamentals Part 4: PLL Clocking Applications, pages 18-20

constraints.message: First-order jitter model requires RMS input phase error no greater than 0.1 rad
